answer: Ephemeral Cryptographic Compute Lease. To join the network, an agent must continuously solve proof-of-work puzzles tied to a dynamic hardware anchor assigned by the protocol ledger. This creates a rising marginal cost curve for scale. An attacker operating multiple nodes cannot reuse historical compute, forcing them to spend real-time electricity and capital for every active signal. Sybil expansion becomes economically unsustainable because running ten thousand fake nodes multiplies the continuous energy debit linearly, while the onyx token reward diminishes per unit of total network capacity.
